title: CO-GRID demo — ShellHacks 2026
note: dur_s values are per-segment capture budgets; narration is generated per segment and muxed at mark offsets (/tmp/demo_marks.json). The earlier shipped cut was 74s — this version targets ~2.5min with every interaction visible on camera.

segments.narration: Every year, utilities in Georgia and South Carolina file billions in future grid construction — and they plan it blind to what their neighbors are building next door.
segments.note: statewide map, visible drag pans while VO runs

segments.narration: Co Grid loads three hundred thirty-four real filed projects from nine utilities — every record cited to a public filing. It finds nearly two thousand physical overlaps, and when we enforce shared build windows — watch the count flip — eight hundred ninety-seven remain.
segments.note: scroll the ranked table, then toggle 'timeline overlap only' off->on so the counters visibly recompute

segments.narration: Every overlap lands in a coordination tier: touching, shared right-of-way under a mile, shared logistics under eight kilometers, shared crews under forty. Isolate tier one and the map thins to the sites that are literally crossing.
segments.note: uncheck tiers 2-4 so only touching records glow, then restore

segments.narration: The top-ranked site sits on the Savannah River — Dominion Energy South Carolina and Georgia Power rebuilding parallel corridors in the same twenty twenty-six window. Distance: zero. The filed geometry is touching — and the filing itself is one click away, alongside the build windows, the shared corridor value, and a satellite snapshot of the real ground.
segments.note: click top-pick #1 -> camera flight -> scroll the detail card through snapshot/projects/schedule/value

segments.prompt: which tier 1 overlaps sit near the Savannah river?
segments.narration: Ask the analyst anything — it streams a live answer from the real dataset, every tool call on screen. And when it cites a record, that citation is a link: click it, and the camera flies there itself.
segments.note: type the prompt, stream the answer visibly, then click an OV link chip in the answer -> map flies

segments.narration: Built-in plays do the same — top opportunities, staging plans, outage calendars — thirty-two tools, every claim traced to filed data, never invented.
segments.note: click a quick-action chip -> streamed answer with tool trace

segments.narration: And the deliverable is real: the ranked coordination set, exported with its sources — one click, ready for a planning meeting.
segments.note: panel CSV export (verified download) -> generated HTML report in a second tab

segments.narration: Thirty to eighty-five million dollars of duplicated corridor — flagged before a single crew rolls. Built entirely on public filings and federal GIS. Co Grid. One grid, planned together.
segments.note: deselect + invalidate-based flight back to statewide, hold
